issue.title: ellswift: header says `secp256k1_ellswift_create` is constant time in auxrnd32, but the code is not
issue.body:
The header of `secp256k1_ellswift_create` says (`include/secp256k1_ellswift.h:139`):

> Constant time in seckey and auxrnd32, but not in the resulting public key.

The code is constant time in `seckey32`, but not in `auxrnd32`. `ctime_tests` does not catch it because it marks only the key secret: its two calls pass `NULL` and the public `ellswift` buffer as `auxrnd32` (`src/ctime_tests.c:314,319`).

In `src/modules/ellswift/main_impl.h`, `seckey32` and 32 zero bytes fill the 64-byte block after the tagged-hash midstate, so that block is compressed into `hash.s` (455-456; `src/hash_impl.h:43-48`, `:220-225`). Line 458 then declassifies `hash.s` only:

```c
/* Declassify only hash state. seckey32 has been hashed, but copy remains in the hash buffer */
```

`auxrnd32` is written after that, into `hash.buf` (459), and is compressed only inside `secp256k1_ellswift_prng` (310-325). The branch pool (349) and each `u` (356) are PRNG outputs. `secp256k1_ellswift_xswiftec_inv_var` branches on them (198, 256), and the loop stops at the first accepted candidate (365).

I added a call that marks `auxrnd32` secret too ([b72730b](https://github.com/fametrano/secp256k1/commit/b72730b40fbdc7cfcbc737feb91d7863fda1ede4), [CI run](https://github.com/fametrano/secp256k1/actions/runs/38139414944)). 70 jobs fail on their `ctime_tests` run: 66 run it under Valgrind and exit 42, 4 under MSan and exit 1. All 70 have the ellswift module on, and `make check` passes in each (`# FAIL: 0`). The 4 jobs that run `ctime_tests` with ellswift off pass. From one MSan job, addresses trimmed:

```text
WARNING: MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value
    #0 in secp256k1_ellswift_xswiftec_inv_var src/modules/ellswift/main_impl.h:198:9
    #1 in secp256k1_ellswift_xelligatorswift_var src/modules/ellswift/main_impl.h:365:13
```

On timing I can argue only from the code. The output holds only the accepted `u` and `t`, and the rejected candidates are other SHA256 outputs of the same inputs. I don't see how they would reveal `seckey32` or `auxrnd32` without inverting SHA256, but I have not proven it.

I see two options:

1. Weaken the header for `auxrnd32`.
2. Keep the header. Declassify each PRNG output in `secp256k1_ellswift_xelligatorswift_var`, as line 458 declassifies a hash of `seckey32`, and mark `auxrnd32` secret in `ctime_tests.c`. I have not tried this. Declassifying `hash.s` again after writing `auxrnd32` would not be enough, since `auxrnd32` is still in `hash.buf`.

Which do you prefer? I can open a PR for either.

*Assisted-by: my usual tools (LLM, Internet, computer). Mistakes are mine.*
